question: What is the primary goal of stock holding conventions in a nursing unit?

options.A: Reducing the salary budget of nursing staff
options.B: Increasing the number of beds in the ward
options.C: Ensuring vital supplies are available when needed

explanation: Stock holding conventions focus mainly on making sure medical items and drugs are always ready for patient care without shortages. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h1)

question: Why must nurses understand basic inventory and stock control principles?

options.A: To design new storage shelves for the hospital
options.B: To negotiate better prices with medical suppliers
options.C: To take over the job of the hospital pharmacist
options.D: To prevent emergency supply shortages on the ward

explanation: Nurses handle ward supplies every day, so knowing stock rules helps them prevent running out of critical items during patient care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h1)

question: Which of the following is considered a consumable medical supply?
explanation: Consumables are single-use items that get thrown away after one application, like syringes and gauze. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h2)

question: How should emergency stock items on a ward be managed differently from regular supplies?

options.A: Ordered only once a year to cut down on paperwork
options.B: Checked daily and replaced immediately after any use
options.C: Stored in a locked room away from all nursing staff
options.D: Kept in open corridors for easy public access

explanation: Emergency items must be ready at a moment's notice, requiring daily checks and instant replenishment if used. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h2)

question: What does the FIFO stock rotation rule stand for?
explanation: FIFO means the items that arrived first on the shelf should be the ones picked and used first. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h3)

question: A nurse receives a fresh batch of IV antibiotics. Where should the nurse place them relative to the older stock already on the shelf?

options.D: In front of the older stock

explanation: Placing new stock behind older stock ensures the older items are picked first, practicing FIFO and preventing expiration. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h3)

question: What does the reorder point represent in inventory management?

options.A: The cost of buying a single medical item
options.B: The date when a medication finally expires
options.C: The maximum number of items a shelf can hold
options.D: The specific stock level that triggers a new order

explanation: The reorder point is the threshold that tells the nurse or storekeeper it is time to buy more supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h4)

question: What happens if a nursing unit allows its stock levels to fall below the minimum safety threshold?

options.A: The storage room becomes much cleaner and easier to clean
options.B: The hospital pharmacy saves a lot of money on bulk purchases
options.C: Expired items automatically get removed from the shelves
options.D: Patients may face dangerous delays in treatment due to shortages

explanation: Falling below minimum safety stock means the ward risks running out of crucial supplies during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h4)

question: What should a nurse do if a sterile instrument pack has a torn or damp wrapper?

options.A: Discard or return the item because sterility is lost
options.B: Wipe the outside with alcohol and place it back on the shelf
options.C: Use it quickly before any dust can settle inside
options.D: Ask another nurse to approve using it for a minor dressing

explanation: Any damage or moisture to a sterile wrapper compromises the barrier, meaning the instruments are no longer safe to use. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: Why must vaccine and medication storage refrigerators have their temperatures checked and recorded regularly?

options.A: To ensure the refrigerator door is locked at all times
options.B: To check if the electricity bill is too high for the ward
options.C: To make sure improper heat does not ruin drug potency
options.D: To calculate how many patients received injections that day

explanation: Many pharmaceutical products degrade quickly if temperatures fluctuate outside the safe cold chain range. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a physical stock audit on a hospital ward?

options.A: To test the clinical skills of newly employed nurses
options.B: To compare actual items on the shelf with recorded inventory
options.C: To clean out the dust from the medication store cupboards
options.D: To dispose of all old equipment regardless of expiry date

explanation: Stock audits involve counting what is physically present to match it with what the logbook says should be there. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: Which of the following is a direct consequence of failing to record items taken from the ward inventory?

options.A: The medications on the shelf will expire much faster than normal
options.B: The hospital will automatically order double the amount needed
options.C: Patients will recover faster because fewer drugs are logged
options.D: Stock counts will not match actual inventory, causing unexpected shortages

explanation: Unrecorded items create hidden inventory gaps, making reorder calculations inaccurate and leading to sudden stockouts. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: What is the correct action when a nurse discovers a box of expired intravenous fluids in the treatment room?

options.A: Donate it to a local clinic outside the hospital system
options.B: Use it quickly for non-critical patients before anyone notices
options.C: Hide it at the back of the cupboard until the next audit
options.D: Remove it from the shelf and follow proper waste disposal protocols

explanation: Expired items must be isolated and disposed of safely to ensure they are never accidentally given to a patient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to keep expired medication anywhere near active stock supplies?

options.A: It creates a high risk of accidentally administering degraded drugs to a patient
options.B: It automatically invalidates the expiry dates of neighboring boxes
options.C: It takes up space that should be used for cleaning supplies
options.D: It causes the electric lights in the storage room to flicker

explanation: Closeness to active stock increases the chance that a busy nurse will grab an expired item during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h7)
